text: What is the probability of rolling a sum of 7 with two fair six-sided dice?
explanation: There are 36 equally likely ordered outcomes. Six sum to 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1). Therefore 6/36 = 1/6.

text: Two fair dice are rolled. Given that their sum is at least 10, what is the probability the sum is exactly 12?
explanation: Sums 10, 11, 12 have 3, 2, 1 outcomes respectively, for six equally likely conditioned outcomes. Only (6,6) sums to 12: 1/6.

text: A test has 90% sensitivity and 80% specificity. Prevalence is 10%. What is P(condition | positive)?
explanation: P(positive and condition)=0.9×0.1=0.09. P(positive)=0.09+0.2×0.9=0.27. Bayes gives 0.09/0.27=1/3.

text: A fair six-sided die pays its face value in dollars. What is the expected payout?
explanation: The six outcomes are equally likely. (1+2+3+4+5+6)/6 = 21/6 = 3.5.

text: Two cards are drawn without replacement from a 52-card deck. What is the probability both are aces?
explanation: P(first ace)=4/52; P(second ace | first)=3/51. Multiply to get 12/2652=1/221.

text: Flip a fair coin 4 times. What is the probability of exactly 2 heads?
explanation: Choose which two flips are heads: C(4,2)=6. Each sequence has probability 1/16. Hence 6/16=3/8=0.375.

text: A fair coin is flipped until the first head. What is the expected number of flips?
explanation: The geometric distribution with success probability p has mean 1/p. With p=1/2, E[T]=2.

text: Roll two independent fair dice. What is the variance of their sum?
explanation: A fair die has variance (6²−1)/12=35/12. Independent variances add, giving 2×35/12=35/6.

text: Choose a point uniformly in the unit square. What is the probability x+y < 1?
explanation: The feasible region is a right triangle with legs 1 and 1, area 1/2. The square has area 1, so probability = 1/2.

text: Three fair coins are flipped. Given at least one head, what is the probability all three are heads?
explanation: Eight equally likely sequences exist; exclude TTT, leaving seven with at least one head. Only HHH qualifies: 1/7.

text: Four independent fair coins are flipped. What is the probability of exactly three heads?
explanation: There are 2^4=16 equally likely sequences. Choose the three head positions in C(4,3)=4 ways, giving 4/16=1/4.

text: Roll two fair dice. What is the probability their product is even?
hint: Use the complement: both dice odd.
explanation: A product is odd only when both dice are odd. Each die has 3 odd faces, so P(both odd)=9/36. Thus P(even product)=27/36=3/4.

text: Draw three cards without replacement from a standard 52-card deck. What is the probability all three cards are hearts?
hint: Multiply the conditional probabilities of three hearts.

text: A fair die is rolled once. Given that the result is even, what is the probability the result exceeds 3?
hint: Condition on the three even outcomes.
explanation: The even results are {2,4,6}, equally likely under the condition. Of these, 4 and 6 exceed 3, giving probability 2/3.

text: One percent of items are defective. A detector flags 95% of defective items and 5% of good items. Given a flag, what is the probability the item is defective?
hint: Calculate defective-and-flagged divided by all flagged.

text: A lottery ticket pays $12 with probability 1/4 and $0 otherwise. What is the expected gross payout in dollars?
explanation: Expected payout is 12×(1/4)+0×(3/4)=3 dollars. This is gross payout, before any ticket cost.

text: A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the variance of its face value?
A biased coin shows heads with probability 0.25 on each independent toss. What is the expected number of tosses until the first head?
hint: Use the mean waiting time 1/p for a geometric variable.
explanation: Each independent toss succeeds with probability 1/4. The geometric waiting time, counting the successful toss, has mean 1/(1/4)=4.

text: A basketball player makes each of four independent shots with probability 3/4. What is the probability of exactly three makes?
explanation: Choose the one miss in four ways, then multiply (3/4)^3(1/4). The result is 4×27/256=27/64.

text: Calls arrive as a Poisson process at rate 2 per hour. What is the probability of zero calls in 30 minutes?
explanation: The expected count in half an hour is 2×0.5=1. For a Poisson(1) count, P(N=0)=e^(-1), approximately 0.367879.

text: Two independent uniform random variables on [0,1] are drawn. What is the expected maximum?
explanation: P(max≤x)=x² for 0≤x≤1, so E[max]=integral from 0 to 1 of (1−x²) dx=1−1/3=2/3.

text: Events A and B are independent with P(A)=0.4 and P(B)=0.3. What is P(A and B)?
explanation: Independence gives P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B)=0.4×0.3=0.12, which is 3/25.

text: In a group, P(A)=0.6, P(B)=0.5, and P(A and B)=0.2. What is P(A or B)?
hint: Add marginal probabilities and subtract overlap.
explanation: Inclusion-exclusion says P(A∪B)=0.6+0.5−0.2=0.9. Subtract the overlap once to avoid double counting.

text: A two-state Markov chain switches state with probability 0.2 each step. Starting in state A, what is the probability of being in A after two steps?
hint: Either stay twice or switch twice.
explanation: Return to A by staying both times (0.8²=0.64) or switching both times (0.2²=0.04). Total 0.68=17/25.

text: A bag contains 5 red and 3 blue balls. Draw two without replacement. What is the probability the colors differ?
A symmetric random walk takes four independent steps of +1 or −1. What is the probability it returns to zero?
hint: Returning requires two steps in each direction.
explanation: Exactly two of four steps must be +1. There are C(4,2)=6 such paths out of 2^4=16 equally likely paths, so 6/16=3/8.

text: A factory uses machine A for 70% of parts (2% defective) and machine B for 30% (5% defective). What is the overall defect probability?
hint: Weight each defect rate by production share.

text: X is uniform on [2,8]. What is P(X>5)?
hint: Take the favorable interval length divided by total length.
explanation: The uniform density is constant on an interval of length 6. The portion above 5 has length 8−5=3, so probability 3/6=1/2.

text: Independent fair coin indicators X and Y equal 1 on heads, 0 on tails. What is Cov(X,Y)?
hint: Use independence of the two indicators.
explanation: Independence implies E[XY]=E[X]E[Y]=1/4. Therefore Cov(X,Y)=1/4−(1/2)(1/2)=0.

text: A fair die is rolled until a 6 appears. What is the probability the first 6 occurs on the third roll?
explanation: The first two rolls must be non-6 (probability 5/6 each), followed by a 6 (probability 1/6). Multiply to get 25/216.
